questions.stem: The 'Pahari' school of Indian miniature painting flourished in the hill areas of which region?
questions.explanation: Pahari ('of the hills') miniatures — 17th to 19th century — flourished in the former hill princely states of Kangra, Basohli, Chamba, Guler, Garhwal, Nurpur, Mandi and Mankot, today in Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and parts of J&K. Kangra style (late 18th century) is especially famous for lyrical depictions of Krishna-Radha and the Gita Govinda.

questions.stem: 'Madhubani' painting, known for its brilliant colours and geometric motifs, is a folk tradition of:
questions.explanation: Madhubani (also called Mithila painting) is the folk tradition of the Mithila region of northern Bihar (and southern Nepal). Traditionally done by women on walls and floors of homes for weddings and festivals using natural pigments. Now also on paper and cloth. Famous practitioners — Sita Devi, Ganga Devi, Mahasundari Devi. Awarded GI tag in 2007.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the folk-painting tradition with its state. A. Warli. B. Kalamkari. C. Pattachitra. D. Phad. List-II: 1. Maharashtra, 2. Andhra Pradesh / Telangana, 3. Odisha, 4. Rajasthan.
questions.explanation: Warli — Maharashtra tribal art with geometric white figures on earthen walls. Kalamkari — AP/Telangana, pen-drawn narrative cloth paintings (Sri Kalahasti, Machilipatnam). Pattachitra — Odisha, painted cloth panels with Jagannath themes. Phad — Rajasthan, large scrolls narrating folk epics like Pabuji-ki-phad. Other regional styles — Tanjore (TN), Mysore (Karnataka), Cheriyal scrolls (Telangana).

questions.stem: The Ajanta cave paintings, a glorious chapter in Indian art history, depict scenes mostly from the life of:
questions.explanation: Ajanta caves (Aurangabad district, Maharashtra) — 30 rock-cut Buddhist monasteries dating from about the 2nd century BCE to the 6th century CE. The murals depict scenes from the Buddha's life and the Jataka tales (his past lives). UNESCO WHS 1983. Ellora caves (nearby) contain Buddhist, Hindu and Jain monuments including the huge rock-cut Kailasa temple. Jataka stories.

questions.stem: The Mughal school of miniature painting was founded during the reign of Humayun but reached its peak under:
questions.explanation: Akbar's court (1556-1605) set up a major painting atelier (tasveer khana) and commissioned illustrated manuscripts like the Akbarnama and Hamzanama; his atelier blended Persian, Indian and European influences. Jahangir (1605-27) was a connoisseur and preferred natural-history subjects and portraits (Mansur was his leading painter). Mughal painting declined under Aurangzeb's orthodoxy.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Raja Ravi Varma (1848-1906), one of India's most famous modern painters, is especially known for:

options.option_text: Oil paintings of Hindu mythological scenes

questions.explanation: Ravi Varma was a pioneer of Western-style oil painting in India and became famous for his dramatic canvases of Hindu mythological scenes — 'Shakuntala', 'Damayanti and the Swan', 'Ravana abducting Sita'. He also produced striking realistic portraits. He opened a lithographic press near Mumbai so that inexpensive prints of his paintings could reach ordinary homes, shaping popular iconography of Hindu gods.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The painter M. F. Husain, one of the founders of the Bombay Progressive Artists' Group, is sometimes referred to as the:

options.option_text: Leader of the Bengal School of Art

questions.explanation: M. F. Husain (1915-2011) — known for bold, angular, often colour-drenched works — was often called the 'Picasso of India'. He co-founded the Progressive Artists' Group in Bombay in 1947 with F. N. Souza and others. Controversial paintings of Hindu deities led to his self-exile in 2006; he died in London in 2011 after accepting Qatari citizenship. Dadasaheb Phalke — 'Father of Indian cinema'; Abanindranath Tagore — Bengal School.
